post.summary: Register a new user after Firebase signup
post.description:
Create a user record in the database after successful Firebase signup.

This endpoint should be called by the mobile app immediately after
createUserWithEmailAndPassword succeeds in Firebase.

# TODO: Add email verification flow using Firebase sendEmailVerification

Idempotent endpoint to ensure the authenticated user exists in our database.

- If user exists, returns their info
- If user doesn't exist, creates them and returns their info

Call this once after sign-in to ensure the user is set up before making
other API calls (like requesting upload URLs).

post.summary: Register a new web user with an invite code
post.description:
Server-side web registration.

Validates the invite code, creates the Firebase user, creates the DB
user, and joins the org — all before returning.  Every request takes
at least ``_WEB_REGISTER_MIN_DURATION_S`` to respond regardless of
outcome, preventing timing-based information leakage and brute-force
spam.
Publish a normalized app.opened event for downstream partner delivery.

delete.description:
Permanently delete the current user's account.

This action:
- Anonymizes the user's email and personal information
- Disables the account (login will no longer work)
- Deletes the Firebase authentication account

Recorded videos and associated metadata are retained as they are
company-owned per the Terms of Use, but all personally identifiable
information is removed.

This action cannot be undone.

get.description:
List users in an organization with optional pagination and search.

Only accessible by org admins and data overlords.

- `q`: Search by email (case-insensitive, requires 2+ chars)
- `limit`: If provided, returns paginated results with `hasMore` and `nextOffset`.
- `sort`: 'email' for alphabetical, 'last_upload' for recent activity first (default),
          'duration' or 'uploads' for sorting by upload stats.
- `sort_direction`: 'asc' or 'desc' for the selected sort.
- `start_date`/`end_date`: Filter to users with uploads in date range. When set,
  only users with uploads in the range are returned. Upload stats reflect the period.
- `include_upload_stats`: When false, still returns `lastUploadCreatedAt` for ordering
  but skips `uploadCount` and `totalDurationMs` in the response.
- `include_quality`: When true, each row carries a `quality` summary (user state plus
  the overall tier value and label). Rows without a stored score still return the
  user state.
- `include_feedback`: When true, each row with recorded external-review feedback
  carries a `feedback` summary (total count plus the latest items). Rows without
  feedback return null.
- If `limit` is omitted, returns all users (backwards compatible).

Special case: org_key="public" returns users with uploads that have no organization.

post.description:
Generate per-blob signed URLs for uploading files to a recording session.

Each URL is scoped to a specific blob path, providing true path-level security.
The user can only upload to the exact paths returned.

Path structure: {org_resource_key or 'public'}/{user.resource_key}/{session_id}/{relative_path}
Flat mobile chunk filenames like {log_id}.mp4 are rewritten server-side to
chunk-scoped paths like {log_id}/{log_id}.mp4 before signing.

get.description:
Return the canonical ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country list.

The list is derived from the `iso3166` package and changes only when
that dependency is upgraded. Clients can cache aggressively.

Return the subdivisions selectable for state-level geo gating.

Backed by the bundled boundary dataset, so the list is exactly what the
gate can enforce and what the org `allowedSubdivisions` write API accepts.
Countries without bundled boundaries return an empty list, signalling that
subdivision gating is unavailable for them. Clients can cache aggressively.

RecordingAuthorization.title: RecordingAuthorization
RecordingAuthorization.description:
Explicit gate verdict the client keys on for recording and uploads.

Computed at each decision point (manual hold, geo policy, quota) so the
verdict is authoritative — including REQUIRES_LOCATION, which no
`blocked_reason` string can express. The legacy `can_upload` flag is derived
from this verdict for clients that predate it.

RecordingAuthorizationBlockedReason.title: RecordingAuthorizationBlockedReason
RecordingAuthorizationBlockedReason.description:
Why a recording/upload gate denied access, when the verdict is not APPROVED.

Wire values are the lowercase strings clients already key on. A StrEnum so it
compares equal to and formats as those strings, keeping the API contract byte-
for-byte identical while giving the server a closed vocabulary to switch on.
Only meaningful alongside a non-APPROVED `RecordingAuthorization`.

TaskTranslationEntry.description:
Per-locale task overrides.

Every field is optional; a missing field falls back to the en base column at
read time. `instructions` overrides instructions.text only (the other
instructions fields are behavioral config, identical in every locale). Tags
are intentionally excluded — localized categories are resolved server-side
from the English values (see app.schemas.categories), so the server never
stores localized tags.
